text: Working with APIs is an essential skill for modern developers. An API allows two programs to communicate with each other. To get data, your application sends HTTP requests to a server, and the server usually responds with JSON, a lightweight format that is easy to read and parse. However, before you can access the data, you often need authentication, such as an API key, to prove your identity. You should also respect rate limits, which restrict how many requests you can make in a certain time. Finally, good error handling is important, so your application can respond properly when something goes wrong.
